title: The collaborative mosaic detail screen offers the mosaic's OWNER a "Join mosaic" button
reasoning: Every element of the claim is present and correct. localMosaicProjectForHubProvider exists at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/collaborative_sky/collaborative_sky_providers.dart:30 and resolves mosaicProjectsDaoProvider.getByHubMosaicId (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/mosaic_projects_dao.dart:111) — the same join key CollaborativeMosaicService.joinMosaicAsParticipant reads at collaborative_mosaic_service.dart:203. The three-way branch in _JoinMosaicButtonState.build (collab_mosaic_detail_screen.dart:318-372) produces 'Your mosaic'/'Open the local project' for collab_role 'owner', "You've joined this mosaic"/'Open the local project' for any other local mirror, and only the no-mirror case keeps 'Join mosaic'. The snackbar suppression is real (wasLinked captured before the await, detail screen:405-411) and factually correct because joinMosaicAsParticipant returns the existing id at line 204-205 without touching the hub. The provider is in collaborativeMosaicStateProviders (providers:49) and that list is dropped by mosaic_project_controller.dart:985 onHubStateChanged (publish) and by the screen's own join/refresh paths. Residual considered and rejected as a defect: the CTA is still disabled when canJoin is false (NetworkBackend/DisconnectedBackend) even in the owner branch, but a remote client's local DAO cannot hold the host's project so it never reaches the owner branch, and DisconnectedBackend is the mobile default where the same is true.

Severed the production wiring by forcing isOwner=false and alreadyLinked=false while leaving the provider watch in place: all 3 tests went red (owner and participant cases found 'Join mosaic'; stranger case found 0). Restored; git diff --stat back to 168 insertions / 25 deletions.

title: The Mosaic projects list has no way to create a mosaic and no back affordance
reasoning: Both halves are in the code. _BackBar (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/mosaic/mosaic_projects_list_screen.dart:122-176) is rendered in BOTH branches of build — the NetworkBackend host-only state (line 29) and the local state (line 58) — and because the local branch puts every list sub-state (loading/empty/error/populated) inside the Expanded below it, the bar covers all of them, not just the populated one. _leave pops when canPop and otherwise context.go('/analytics'), so it is never inert. The 'New mosaic' action is a ScreenHeader trailing SkotiqButton opening the same MosaicWizardDialog the sequencer uses, and MosaicWizardDialog._persistProject (mosaic_wizard_dialog.dart:581-607) really does create the row, Navigator.pop() the dialog and context.push('/mosaic/$projectId'), so the loop closes. Checked for the header-overflow shape that bit another fix this wave: ScreenHeader is a Row of icon + Expanded(title/subtitle) + trailing with soft-wrapping Text, so the extra trailing child cannot overflow horizontally. Two inaccuracies in the fixer's own comment that are not behavioural defects: /mosaic is a child of the ShellRoute (app_router.dart:91/288), so the screen is NOT chromeless — the app shell's nav is present; and opening the wizard from here supplies no initialRa/initialDec so the design starts at RA 0h Dec 0deg until the operator drags or types a centre (the Advanced centre fields and onDragCenter exist, so it is reachable).
evidence: test/screens/mosaic/ runs 55/55 green including the new mosaic_projects_list_actions_test.dart (back control on both states, New mosaic opens MosaicWizardDialog with the create button present). Severed by wrapping both _BackBar call sites in `if (false)`: 2 of 3 tests went red ('Found 0 widgets' for byTooltip('Back') on both the populated and remote states). Restored; diff --stat back to 74 insertions / 6 deletions.

title: Flat wizard tutorial GlobalKeys were attached to three simultaneously-mounted tabs (found while testing)
reasoning: The claim is accurate down to the detail. FlatWizardTutorialKeys.filterSelect/targetAdu/frameCount were attached unconditionally by both _BatchCaptureControls and _SkyFlatsControls, and startBtn by the single _ActionButtons that all three tabs mount (capture_mode_controls.dart:61/126/211 pass mode: quick/batch/skyFlats). All six shared-key sites are now gated on `isSelected` (state.mode == this tab's mode) and startBtn on `mode == state.mode`. The gate cannot strand the tutorial: state.mode is only ever moved by _onTabChanged (flat_wizard_screen.dart:44-51) from the same TabController that drives the TabBarView, and it is deliberately deferred until indexIsChanging clears, so during the switch the OUTGOING tab still owns the keys and the incoming one does not — exactly one claimant in every frame. Pre-existing behaviour is not regressed: TabBarView only builds the visible page at rest, so a key belonging to an unselected tab was already unreachable before the fix.
evidence: The fix shipped NO test, so I added packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/flat_wizard/flat_wizard_tab_switch_test.dart, which pumps FlatWizardScreen at 1280x900 and walks Batch -> Sky Flats -> Quick -> Sky Flats asserting takeException() is null. Green with the fix. Reverting the six gates to the unconditional keys makes it red on the first switch with the exact framework error: 'Duplicate GlobalKey detected in widget tree ... [GlobalKey#3f73d flat_start_btn]'. Restored the production files byte-for-byte (diff --stat unchanged). Note on the 2 failures in test/screens/flat_wizard/: they are captures_landscape_test.dart golden pixel diffs, and the identical failure reproduces on dashboard/ and weather/ captures_landscape_test.dart which this wave never touched (40-47% diff), i.e. the known Linux-vs-Windows golden baseline problem, not a regression.

title: All-Sky alignment shows a drift-derived error with no indication of how long the drift baseline is
reasoning: The caption exists and is wired (_right_panel.dart:124-126 gated on isAllSky, _buildDriftBaselineCaption + formatDriftBaseline in polar_alignment_error_format.dart:38), state.initialError really is latched on the first error event of the adjusting phase (polar_alignment_provider.dart:278-282), and the reticle-overflow half is real and tested (the 160*textScale floor in _right_panel plus all_sky_reticle_layout_test.dart's squeezed-panel case). But the central claim - 'computed from the exact interval the misalignment was derived over' - is false. The native run solves ONE baseline frame in do_baseline (all_sky_polar/mod.rs:198-218) and computes every reading as compute_polar_misalignment_from_drift(&baseline, &current) (mod.rs:265). The first ERROR event is emitted only after the adjustment loop's first cadence sleep + capture + solve (mod.rs:232-278), and PolarAlignmentError.fromEventData stamps timestamp: DateTime.now() on receipt, so the app's initialError is one full iteration LATER than the baseline frame. The caption therefore understated the true drift interval by cadence (default 3.0s, polar_alignment_config.dart:143) + exposure + solve on every sample, and printed a flat 'Drift baseline: 0s' for a first reading actually derived over ~10s. The fixer also explicitly leaves the second half of the finding undone (withholding the green 'Within acceptance' verdict below a minimum baseline), so the finding is self-declared partial.
evidence: test/screens/polar_alignment/ runs 45 pass / 2 fail; both failures are captures_landscape_test.dart golden pixel diffs that reproduce identically on dashboard/ and weather/ captures_landscape_test.dart (40-47% diff on screens this wave never touched) - the known Linux-vs-Windows baseline problem, not a regression. Traced the anchor through all_sky_polar/mod.rs do_baseline/do_adjustment and bridge/src/api/polar_alignment.rs:1445 (every all-sky status is emitted with phase 'adjusting', so the app cannot even distinguish the baseline step from the loop).
repairSummary: Rewrote _buildDriftBaselineCaption so the panel stops asserting a precision it does not have: a single drift solve now reads 'Drift baseline: first drift solve' instead of the untrue '0s', and a longer run reads 'Drift baseline: at least 4m 12s' - a floor, which is what the app can actually prove. Corrected the doc comment, which asserted the interval was exact. Updated the existing expectation in polar_alignment_wizard_ux_test.dart and added a new case, 'the first All-Sky drift solve is not called a 0s baseline', that fails if the bare gap is printed again. dart format clean; polar suite 45 green.

title: Starting a co-imaging session makes you type RA and Dec by hand with no target lookup
reasoning: Every load-bearing claim checks out. _CoordinateSources (coimaging_create_sheet.dart:377-427) is rendered directly under the Target-name field (line 215-219) with 'Look up coordinates' (enabled at name.length >= 2) and 'From mount' (enabled only when mountStateProvider reports connected AND non-null ra/dec, with the disabled Tooltip giving the reason). _LookupResults (line 435-504) watches the real targetCoordinateLookupProvider from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/target_node_properties/coordinate_lookup.dart, which is genuinely two-source (NetworkBackend.searchTargets or targetsDaoProvider, then CatalogManager.instance.search) and swallows a per-source failure so one source cannot mask the other. Both unit conversions are correct and independently confirmed: TargetCoordinateMatch.raHours is hours (the catalog branch divides result.ra by 15 with a comment saying CatalogSearchResult is degrees) and MountState.ra is hours (annotation_pipeline.dart:160 '`mountState.ra` is HOURS (ASCOM RightAscension)'), so both apply paths multiply by 15 into this form's degrees field. Both fields stay editable (plain controllers, no readOnly). The fixer's aside that the finding missed the existing prefill is true: `git show HEAD:...collaborative_sky_screen.dart` already passed initialTargetName/initialRaDeg from framingProvider at line 346-347 before this wave. No second create surface exists to miss - coImagingSessionServiceProvider.createSession has exactly one UI caller in skotiq_app (this sheet), reached from both collaborative_sky_screen and shared_target_detail_screen. Checked the overflow shape too: SkotiqDialogSurface wraps the body in a SingleChildScrollView (skotiq_dialog.dart:230-232) and the result list is height-capped at 170, so the two extra rows cannot overflow the phone bottom sheet. The only residual is the layering smell the fixer already documents (the resolver still lives in the sequencer's Target-editor part file and is imported here with a `show`), which is not a behavioural defect.
evidence: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/collaborative_sky/ runs 60/60 green including the new coimaging_create_sources_test.dart. Severed the production wiring by wrapping the _CoordinateSources call site in `if (false)` while leaving _applyMatch/_applyMountPosition/_LookupResults intact: all 3 tests went red (00:01 +0 -3). Restored; git diff --stat back to 193 insertions / 3 deletions.

title: The mosaic collaborative card never said how many panels THIS rig is holding
reasoning: The line is real (mosaic_project_screen.dart:761-771 renders 'You hold ${state.heldPanelCount} of ${state.panels.length} panels · ${state.panelsUploaded} uploaded to the hub'), and the fixer's load-bearing provenance claim is TRUE and I verified it end to end: a local claim_token is only ever written by _panelsDao.setClaim after this device's own client.claimPanel succeeded (collaborative_mosaic_service.dart:271-277), joinMosaicAsParticipant mirrors a peer's panels with NO token (service:220-227), and refreshStatus only syncs the mosaic's lifecycle string (service:583-590) — so nothing writes another rig's claim into the local row and the count really is 'mine'. What is wrong is the arithmetic: heldPanelCount was `panels.length - unclaimedPanels.length`, i.e. every panel carrying a token, INCLUDING ones this rig has already uploaded. The hub treats an uploaded panel as spent — MosaicBrokerService.claimPanel returns null for status 'uploaded' ('an uploaded panel is done — never re-claimable', mosaic_broker_service.dart:172-173) and releasePanel refuses anything not still 'claimed' (line 217) — and the app already agrees with that everywhere else: mosaic_panel_grid.dart:161-164 hides Release for `isClaimed && isUploaded`, and mosaic_project_controller.dart:352 drops claimExpiresAt using exactly `panels.any((p) => p.isClaimed && !p.isUploaded)`. So a rig that claimed 3 of 9 panels and delivered all 3 read 'You hold 3 of 9 panels · 3 uploaded to the hub' directly above the no-active-claim caption 'A claimed panel is held for your rig until you release it or the hub claim expires' — the card contradicting itself and offering the operator outstanding work (and a hand-back) that does not exist. That is the relocated-false-claim shape this campaign keeps hitting: the old number was uninformative but true; the new one is informative and wrong in the common end state. The shipped test only covered claimed-and-not-uploaded, which is the one case where the two definitions agree. NOT repaired (out of scope, pre-existing, and not confined): the hub expires a claim after a 12h TTL and nothing clears or renews the local claim_token, so the held count can also go stale-true after a long gap; fixing that needs hub-state reconciliation in collaborative_mosaic_service, which other areas share.
evidence: Repaired then revert-checked. With the fix, test/screens/mosaic/ is 56/56 green (was 55 before my added case). Reverting heldPanelCount to `panels.length - unclaimedPanels.length` makes only the new case red — '00:01 +6 -1: an uploaded panel is no longer counted as held [E]' — while the fixer's own 'the card says how many panels THIS rig is holding' stays green both ways, which is precisely why the gap survived. Restored; suite back to 56 green. dart format clean on all three files.
repairSummary: Redefined MosaicProjectState.heldPanelCount (mosaic_project_controller.dart:127-140) as `panels.where((p) => p.isClaimed && !p.isUploaded).length` — the same outstanding-claim set the per-panel Release button and the claim-expiry caption already use — and documented why an uploaded panel is excluded (the hub refuses to release or re-open it). Retuned the screen's comment to say the count is outstanding work, not lifetime assignment. Added 'an uploaded panel is no longer counted as held' to mosaic_project_screen_collab_test.dart: two claimed panels, one uploaded, asserting 'You hold 1 of 3 panels' and NOT 'You hold 2 of 3 panels'; it fails when the fix is reverted.
